items.q: Explain why the sky is blue.
items.text: The blue colouration of the sky is attributable to Rayleigh scattering, a phenomenon whereby shorter wavelengths of solar radiation are dispersed by atmospheric molecules to a substantially greater degree than longer wavelengths. Consequently, an observer perceives a predominance of blue light.

items.q: Explain why the sky is blue.
items.text: Sunlight contains many wavelengths. As it passes through the atmosphere, shorter wavelengths such as blue are scattered by gas molecules more than longer wavelengths. This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from all directions, so the sky appears blue.
